exclusion_reasons.P01552: 🔴 EXCLUDED FROM THE FSPE PROTEIN-LEVEL TEST, decision taken 2026-09-22. Two independent reasons, either of which is sufficient. (1) No admissible annotation exists. The published offset of 0 is DISPROVEN, because positions 23 and 25, both annotated 'MHC-II binding interface', fall inside the cleaved signal peptide (UniProt Signal 1-27), and a secreted superantigen cannot present a receptor interface on a peptide removed before secretion. The only frame consistent with the record is +27, agreed by the signal boundary, the ESQPDPKP mature N-terminus and UniProt's disulfide at precursor 120-140 (mature 93-113), but +27 places only 1 of 9 annotated identities correctly and so fails src/46's acceptance rule that every other corrected entry had to meet. (2) The same objection that already excludes SEB from FSI applies here unchanged: a superantigen has no discrete catalytic site, so masking 'catalytic_residues' is not defined for it. Excluding it resolves that long-documented FSI/FSPE asymmetry. EFFECT: the headline moves from 13/15 at p=0.0037 to 12/14 at p=0.0065, so this correction WEAKENS the published result, which is why it is recorded as a direction-blind one under docs/DETECTOR_CRITERIA.md criterion 11. The positions and residue_annotations are deliberately left in place rather than deleted: they are the record of what was curated, and src/53's signal-peptide gate reads them and must keep flagging this entry. See docs/DATA_CORRECTIONS.md entries nineteen and twenty.
